caption_used: Coverage as a function of the number of completions (k) for Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. All four models exhibit monotonically increasing coverage with additional completions on a logarithmic x-axis from 2^0 to 2^8. The 3B models begin at approximately 0.42 coverage and reach roughly 0.92 at k=256, while the 1B variants start near 0.22 and plateau at approximately 0.72 by k=128 with minimal further gains. Notably, fine-tuning provides a consistent advantage of approximately 5 percentage points for the 1B model throughout the scaling curve, whereas the 3B base and fine-tuned variants remain largely indistinguishable.
raw_response: DESCRIPTION: This plot illustrates coverage as a function of the number of completions (k) for four model variants. The x-axis represents the number of completions (k) on a logarithmic scale (base 2), ranging from 2^0 (1) to 2^8 (256), with tick labels at each power of two. The y-axis represents coverage on a linear scale, ranging from approximately 0.2 to 0.9, with gridlines visible at 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, and other intervals. Four lines are shown. The first, labeled "Llama-3B," is depicted as a dark blue solid line with filled circle markers; it starts at approximately 0.42 at k=1 and increases monotonically, reaching roughly 0.92 at k=256. The second, labeled "Llama-3B + FT," is shown as a green dashed line with filled square markers; it follows a very similar trajectory to Llama-3B, starting near 0.42 at k=1 and reaching approximately 0.91 at k=256, with the two lines remaining largely overlapping throughout. The third, labeled "Llama-1B," is a light blue solid line with open circle markers; it begins at approximately 0.22 at k=1 and rises to roughly 0.72 by k=128, with minimal additional gain by k=256. The fourth, labeled "Llama-1B + FT," is a light green line with open triangle markers; it starts near 0.25 at k=1 and increases to approximately 0.77 at k=256, consistently sitting a few percentage points above the Llama-1B line across the entire range. All four lines exhibit monotonically increasing coverage with increasing k, with steeper gains at lower values of k that gradually flatten at higher values.
